explanation: A nonempty undirected tree must have V minus one edges and one connected component. Check the edge count, then use disjoint sets to test connectivity.
timeComplexity: O((V + E) log(V + 1)) amortized upper bound with path compression alone.
attribution: Original EPI Practice C# implementation, reusing and refining the repository-authored Blind75 algorithm fixtures. Collection membership follows Crackr; no external solution service is used.
correctness: Every nonempty undirected tree has exactly V-1 edges and is connected. Conversely, a connected undirected graph with V-1 edges has no cycle, so it is a tree. Checking the edge count and then connectivity is therefore necessary and sufficient for this graph contract.
walkthrough: For n=4 and edges [0,1],[1,2],[1,3], there are exactly 3=4-1 edges and every vertex joins the component containing 1. The graph is connected with the required edge count, so return true.
edgeCases: One vertex with no edges is a tree.
The empty graph is not a tree in this collection.
A disconnected graph fails even if its total edge count is V-1.
